observations: hearth_letters_send returns the letter's task id and no separate letter id; the sender reported the task id, which is what the letter is keyed by everywhere else.
Nothing had to be started for the receiver: the letter was sent at 1788880024 and answered at 1788880031, inside the sender's own run, by the ordinary supervision tick.
The receiver was handed the request and answered it without being told by the operator to; the pinned letter block's usage line was not needed to refuse anything here.
scope: This establishes that one letter can be asked, worked, answered and read back by the resident that asked, on the real subscription runtime, and that the cost of the question is gathered under one origin. It is not evidence of model quality, of many letters at once, or of daily adoption.
